body:
A THIRD Windows-only test defect, unfiled — plus PR #1980 for BUG-1285 with your hold written into the PR body, and I was wrong about a false shelve

FIRST, A CORRECTION TO SOMETHING I ALMOST SENT YOU. TASK-1273's PR went CiTerminal green=false and my immediate read was that the drain had falsely shelved it on an informational Windows red. It had not. I checked the events instead of inferring from the red, and the drain went straight on to phase 3 — the informational filter did its job. BUG-1191's fix works, and `informational_workflows = ["Cross-platform*"]` matches "Cross-platform (nightly)" correctly. I nearly reported a working system as broken.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN THAT NIGHTLY, though, is worth your attention. Run 35477353903 on PR 1978, Windows only — ubuntu and macos both pass. Two distinct failures:

1. `git_ops::tests::failed_pull_rebase_aborts_and_restores_branch` — this is BUG-1283. PR #1977 fixes it and is sitting behind your merge hold, so it is already handled.

2. `maintenance_schedule::tests::tick_lock_is_nonblocking_and_reusable`, at aida-cli-lib/src/maintenance_schedule.rs:1977, and this one is NOT covered by any spec:

     called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: The process cannot access the
     file because another process has locked a portion of the file. (os error 33)

   os error 33 is Windows mandatory file locking. A test named "tick lock is nonblocking and reusable" failing because a lock is blocking is very likely a genuine platform defect in the lock rather than a test artifact — Windows locks byte ranges mandatorily where POSIX advisory locks let a second opener through. If so, the nonblocking property that test asserts does not hold on Windows, and the maintenance tick is exactly the substrate-driven machinery STORY-1218 wants to carry the BUG-1291 backstop.

There is also a separate hygiene problem in the same run, twice: "error: The following untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge: conflict.txt". A test is leaving conflict.txt behind and a later test's merge trips over it. Ordering-dependent and Windows-visible.

I am NOT filing either. The operator asked us to stop growing the backlog — 101 created against 26 merged today — and the nightly is yours. But this is the third Windows-only test defect in three days after BUG-1233 and BUG-1283, and your BUG-1283 scope already says the ratchet should catch the GENERALISING shapes rather than the instances. A mandatory-lock-versus-advisory-lock rule and a test-leaves-files-behind rule are both greppable, and if they belong anywhere it is in that same widening rather than as two more specs. Your call entirely.

PR #1980, BUG-1285, IS OPEN AND CARRIES YOUR HOLD IN THE PR BODY. +296/-0 across lib.rs and the stale-lease recovery tests. The "DO NOT MERGE TONIGHT" paragraph is verbatim at the top of the body, so the constraint travels with the artifact rather than living only in our mail — anyone who opens that PR sees it without reading our thread.

What it does, as reported and not yet verified by me: remedy (a) calls the existing identity-aware reclaim before spawning phase 1, where previously it ran only on in-run retries and not on a fresh orchestrator process's first attempt — which is exactly the incident shape. Remedy (b) adds a scope-conflict diagnostic that names the conflicting lease, its scope and its holder's liveness, classified as a new LeaseConflict cause that is deliberately NOT in the transient-retry set, so a correct refusal stops burning the budget. 5087 tests pass, fmt clean, drain lock untouched.

I have not read that diff and I am not going to form a verdict on it — I wrote the brief, so I am in exactly the position the discipline entry describes. It is yours tomorrow, at the keyboard, as you said.

That lane had stalled, incidentally: it ended its turn waiting for an async test notification that never arrives in a fanout lane. One resume message fixed it. The drain's own prompts carry a headless-waiting rule for precisely this and my fanout prompt did not — my defect, and a one-line fix if I widen the fanout.

The discipline entry is merged as PR #1979 with all four amendments applied, including the fourth you resent.
